Over 100 IEDs, weapons, ammunition seized in Teknaf, 2 detained
item.description:
Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) has seized more than 100 improvised explosive devices (IEDs), materials used to make explosives, firearms and a large quantity of ammunition during an operation in Teknaf, Cox’s Bazar.
Two auto-rickshaw drivers were detained, while a motorcycle and two auto-rickshaws allegedly used by the suspects were seized.
Colonel Anwar Ul Alam, sector commander of BGB’s Ramu Sector, confirmed the operation and the seizures on Sunday morning.
According to BGB sources, personnel from the 2nd BGB Battalion under the Ramu Sector conducted the operation based on a tip-off.
The recovered items include a foreign-made pistol, a locally made firearm and 254 rounds of ammunition. The force also seized materials used to manufacture IEDs, including steel casings, electrical wires and specialised toolkits.
The BGB suspects that an organised group had stockpiled the weapons and explosives to carry out acts of sabotage amid the current situation in the country.
According to BGB sources, the group had procured the items from neighbouring Myanmar.
The force believes the IEDs and explosive-making materials were stockpiled for potential sabotage. However, details about the interrogation of the two detainees and their alleged involvement have not yet been disclosed.
Colonel Anwar Ul Alam said legal proceedings were underway over the seizure and the detention of the two individuals.

item.title: Govt revises education allowances for officials’ children abroad
item.description:
The government has revised monthly education allowances for children of government officials and employees working at the country’s diplomatic missions abroad, increasing the financial support according to the location of the mission and the children’s level of education.
The Finance Division issued an order on November 19, setting out revised allowance rates for officials serving in 84 Bangladesh missions abroad.
Under the revised structure, missions have been divided into four categories, with monthly allowances varying according to the cost and location of education.
For missions under category "A", covering 15 missions, the monthly allowance for one child studying up to A-level has been fixed at $250, while the rate for two children is $350. At the university level, the allowance is $250 for one child and $380 for two children.
For category "B", covering 41 missions, the monthly allowance is $210 for one child and $310 for two children at the school level. The corresponding rates for university students are $210 and $320.
For category "C", covering 19 missions, the allowance has been set at $210 for one child and $280 for two children at both school and university levels.
For the remaining nine missions under category "D", the monthly allowance is $200 for one child and $250 for two children at the school level. At the university level, the rates are $210 for one child and $250 for two children.
The order stipulates that the existing arrangement requiring officials and employees to bear 15% of their children’s actual education expenses will remain in force.
It also says where English is not the medium of instruction in a country, but an official arranges English-medium education for their children in another English-speaking country, the prescribed allowance for the relevant mission will apply.
The allowance will be payable for a maximum of two children at a time. No allowance will be provided if a child receives education remotely or through digital platforms instead of attending an educational institution.
The Finance Division said other existing conditions governing education allowances would remain unchanged and the revised order would take effect immediately.

item.title: Workers return to work in Savar-Ashulia, 23 factories remain closed
item.description:
Garment workers returned to their workplaces in Savar and Ashulia on Sunday amid ongoing labour unrest over demands for a minimum wage, with the industrial areas witnessing a largely peaceful start to the second working day of the week.
Workers were seen entering factories as usual in the morning, with no major disturbances reported across the industrial belt.
However, 23 garment factories remained closed following isolated incidents, despite an improvement in the situation compared to the previous day.
Of the factories, 21 were shut under the “no work, no pay” provision in Section 13(1) of the Bangladesh Labour Act, 2006. The remaining two declared general holidays after workers did not report for duty.
Mohammad Mominul Islam Bhuiyan, superintendent of police of Industrial Police-1, confirmed the information.
Industrial Police officials expressed hope that the peaceful situation would continue, although stability would largely depend on workers' participation in production activities.
Meanwhile, law enforcement personnel remained on high alert at key points across the industrial belt and outside factories to prevent any untoward incidents.

item.title: Tribunal to issue order on Masud Uddin’s CMH treatment plea on November 25
item.description:
The hearing on a petition filed by retired lieutenant general Masud Uddin Chowdhury, an accused in a crimes against humanity case, seeking transfer from Dhaka Medical College Hospital (DMCH) to the Combined Military Hospital (CMH) for treatment has concluded.
International Crimes Tribunal-2 on Sunday set November 25 for passing an order on the petition.
During the hearing, Chief Prosecutor Md Aminul Islam told the tribunal that the defence had sought permission for Masud Uddin to receive treatment at CMH.
However, he argued that CMH lacked the necessary security arrangements for patients in the custody of prison authorities. In contrast, Bangladesh Medical University (BMU)—formerly known as Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujib Medical University (BSMMU) and DMCH have facilities for police surveillance to ensure the security of detainees receiving treatment.
He suggested that treatment at either of the two hospitals would therefore be more appropriate.
On November 11, defence counsel Liton Ahmed argued that Masud Uddin had been suffering from blood cancer for a long time and also had kidney complications requiring regular dialysis, as advised by his doctors.
He had also developed heart-related complications and required specialised and continuous medical care, the lawyer said.
Major (retd) Mozaffar Hossain has also been arrested and is being held in connection with the case. The tribunal has directed that investigation reports concerning both accused be submitted by November 23.
According to the prosecution, Mozaffar maintained regular contact with Masud Uddin during the July mass uprising, when a massacre took place in Feni. Investigators have found evidence of their involvement in the incident, the prosecution said.
Earlier, on July 21, the prosecution sought a production warrant to formally show Mozaffar Hossain arrested in the case. He is also an accused in the case over the assassination of former president Ziaur Rahman.
On the night of March 23 this year, the Detective Branch (DB) of police arrested Masud Uddin Chowdhury from his residence in Baridhara DOHS in Dhaka.
He is known as one of the key figures behind the political transition of January 11, 2007, commonly referred to as 1/11.

item.title: PM: Development impossible without SME production, marketing
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has said national development is impossible without production and marketing in the small and medium enterprise (SME) sector, which has played a key role in the progress of many European countries.
Against this backdrop, the government is taking various initiatives to promote SME growth. The draft National SME Policy 2026 is expected to receive Cabinet approval soon, with the aim of transforming Bangladesh into a manufacturing hub and export gateway.
Tarique Rahman made the remarks while inaugurating the National SME Product Fair at the China-Bangladesh Friendship Exhibition Centre in Agargaon, Dhaka, on Sunday.
Organised by the Ministry of Industries under the theme “Prosperity through SMEs, Growth for the Economy”, the fair features 380 entrepreneurs.
The prime minister said the SME sector was a key priority for the government and that there was no alternative to its development in building an economically prosperous country.
However, he identified a lack of capital and technology, difficulties in accessing loans and a shortage of skilled workers as major barriers to SME development, production and marketing.
He said providing loans on favourable terms, offering incentives and promoting public-private partnerships could help address these challenges.
The government aims to increase the SME sector's contribution to the national economy to 35%, a move expected to create 2.5 million jobs, he added.
Industries Minister Khandaker Abdul Muktadir chaired the event, while Finance Minister Amir Khasru Mahmud Chowdhury and FBCCI Administrator Md Fazlul Haque attended as special guests.
Abdun Naser Khan, secretary of the Ministry of Industries and chairperson of the SME Foundation, said developing the SME sector was essential to making Bangladesh's economic growth more inclusive, dynamic and sustainable.

item.title: 95 platoons of BGB deployed in seven districts, including Gopalganj
item.description:
The Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) has deployed 95 platoons across seven districts, including two battalions in Gopalganj, to maintain law and order, ensure public security, and handle any untoward situation.
The deployment, made following instructions from the Ministry of Home Affairs, also covers Dhaka, Narayanganj, Gazipur, Mymensingh, Faridpur and Cox’s Bazar districts, according to a BGB press release issued on Sunday.
The deployed BGB personnel are performing their duties in coordination with the respective district administration and other law enforcement agencies.
Security and surveillance have been strengthened at key installations, industrial areas and other important locations in the districts to prevent disorder, violence and activities that could pose a threat to public security, the release said.
Meanwhile, the BGB headquarters is maintaining technology-based surveillance through its monitoring cell to closely monitor the situation on the ground and ensure coordination.
Live footage collected through drones, body-worn cameras and other modern technologies is being monitored round the clock, according to the release.
It said BGB members were performing their assigned duties in maintaining internal law and order alongside their regular responsibilities at the borders, with the highest level of professionalism, discipline and patience.
The force remained committed to ensuring the safety of people's lives and property, keeping normal movement and daily activities uninterrupted, and taking necessary precautionary measures to deal with any untoward situation, the release added.

item.title: Messi furore after Columbus thrash Miami in MLS Cup
item.description:
Columbus Crew coach Laurent Courtois said Lionel Messi should have been sent off after hurling a throw-in at an opponent as Inter Miami crashed to a 3-0 defeat in the MLS Cup playoffs on Saturday.
Messi's frustration boiled over on the stroke of half-time when he aimed a forceful throw-in into the face of Columbus Crew forward Gonzalo Tapia with 10-man Miami trailing 1-0 at the time.
Messi and Tapia both were shown yellow cards for the incident by referee Allen Chapman, but Courtois said afterwards the Argentina superstar should have been given a red card.
"Everybody knows that he deserved more than a yellow card," Courtois said in a post-game press conference when asked about the incident. "It's just really sad."
Referee Chapman later defended the decision to only show Messi a yellow.
"The force used was negligible and the offense did not reach the level of violent conduct," Chapman told a pool reporter.
Inter Miami had already been reduced to 10 men when the incident occurred and were 1-0 down after Chile international Tapia's early penalty.
Reigning MLS champions Miami went on to suffer a 3-0 defeat, with Tapia grabbing a second after a Taha Habroune strike just after half-time at Miami's Nu Stadium.
The result means seventh seeds Columbus, the 2023 champions, can eliminate Messi and Miami from the playoffs with a victory in game two of the best-of-three series in Ohio next Friday.
"It was a game where nothing went right for us, and we effectively created their chances for them," Miami coach Kily Gonzalez said afterwards.
"We didn't produce the great performance we had hoped for. Everything went wrong, but we have to learn from it because next time, if we don't win, we're out," he added.
"There's no better challenge for us as a team than this. It's a test of character, and I know my team has that character."
In other MLS playoff action on Saturday, Joaquin Valiente scored two goals as host Dallas beat Portland 3-0 in their Western Conference series opener.
The 25-year-old Uruguayan midfielder scored in the 53rd and 55th minutes and Samuel Sarver added an insurance goal in the fourth minute of stoppage time for Dallas, who can advance by winning at Portland next Saturday.
US teen Peyton Miller scored one goal and set up another in New England's 2-0 victory over visiting Philadelphia.
Miller’s 10th-minute shot deflected in off Philadelphia defender Nathan Harriel to make it 1-0 and the 19-year-old scored in the 73rd minute off a Jack Harrison cross to complete the scoring.
New England can advance to the MLS Eastern Conference semi-finals with a road victory next Saturday.

item.title: Pant ton drives India to record 720-9dec against New Zealand
item.description:
India scored the highest innings total in Test matches in New Zealand on Sunday, declaring at a mammoth 720-9 on Sunday midway through the fourth afternoon of the first Test in Wellington, after Rishabh Pant's blistering 128.
New Zealand were 33-1 in their second innings at tea, with captain Tom Latham falling in the first over, needing another 319 runs to avoid an innings defeat with four sessions to go.
Henry Nicholls was 21 not out and Devon Conway on 12 at the break after Latham registered a dreaded "pair" of ducks, out for nought second ball for the second time in the game when he edged Jasprit Bumrah to Pant.
India surpassed the previous record for Tests in New Zealand, the hosts' 715-6 declared against Bangladesh in Hamilton in 2019.
It was the 18th highest innings in Test history.
Dhruv Jurel was the last man out, stumped from the bowling of Glenn Phillips for a brisk 78 off 79 balls.
Pant was the star of the morning, falling off the last ball before lunch as India reached the break on 629-6.
The diminutive wicketkeeper brought up his hundred by lofting Glenn Phillips over long-off for six, before kissing the badge of his helmet and pointing to the sky.
It was his ninth hundred in Test cricket, and included 10 fours and six sixes.
Pant had been 55 not out overnight alongside Anshul Kamboj, who was yet to score but took on the role of aggressor with a flurry of lofted drives and outright slogs.
He fell for a swift 38 from 42 balls, hitting six fours and a six, bringing Dhruv Jurel to the crease and prompting Pant to come out of his shell.
He whacked Phillips out of the Basin Reserve ground, the ball seen running down neighbouring Cambridge Terrace alongside the Sunday morning traffic.
Jurel was 32 not out when Pant was dismissed on the brink of lunch, caught by Nathan Smith at deep midwicket from Rachin Ravindra's bowling after facing 153 balls.
Ravindra ended with 2-44 from 10 overs, while Glenn Phillips took 3-154 in 24 overs.
Seamer Jacob Duffy conceded the second most runs in an innings by a bowler in New Zealand Test history, returning 1-201 from 33 overs.
Each of India's top five batsmen had scores of 80 or higher, the first time that has happened in a Test.
KL Rahul made 136 opening the batting alongside Yashasvi Jaiswal, who made 85.
Devdutt Padikkal scored 80 and Shubman Gill 98, before Pant's hundred on day four.

item.title: Nmecha helps Dortmund beat Gladbach to top Bundesliga
item.description:
Felix Nmecha scored with 10 minutes remaining to send Borussia Dortmund to the top of the Bundesliga table with a 1-0 win at Borussia Moenchengladbach on Saturday.
Bayern Munich's 1-1 home draw with Cologne on Friday opened up the door for the chasers but Dortmund had few opportunities until Nmecha's late strike.
Dortmund are now outright first on 24 points, with Bayern and Freiburg, who won 1-0 at Elversberg, locked on 22 points.
Bayern also lost Harry Kane to injury in Friday's draw, with the Ballon d'Or winner set to miss several months after undergoing surgery on his injured ankle earlier on Saturday.
Dortmund captain Nico Schlotterbeck urged his teammates not to get too far ahead of themselves, despite overtaking Bayern.
"The season is only truly decided from March or April onwards. We need to be in the mix by then," he told reporters.
Dortmund, who travel to Arsenal on Tuesday, knew victory would send them top but the 2024 Champions League finalists had few chances against a stubborn Gladbach.
Nmecha, who scored twice in Dortmund's 2-1 win over Elversberg before the international break, looked most likely when his header forced a save from Daniel Batz.
With 17 minutes left, Marcel Sabitzer chipped a free-kick inches wide of the post.
Dortmund continued to push and Nmecha was on hand to knock a rebound through Batz's fingers and help the visitors snare a crucial three points.
Igor Matanovic's 68th-minute strike helped Freiburg break down promoted Elversberg and move level with Bayern.
Last season's Europa League finalists Freiburg stay one point ahead of fourth-placed RB Leipzig, who romped to a 5-1 victory at Union Berlin.
Antonio Nusa, Romulo, Brajan Gruda, Rocco Reitz and Ridle Baku scored for Leipzig, who host Lens in the Champions League on Tuesday.
Gruda was particularly impressive with a goal and an assist, just days after impressing for Jurgen Klopp's Germany with a goal and two assists versus the Netherlands on the other side of the German capital.
Elsewhere, Afonso Moreira broke his Bundesliga duck with a brace in Bayer Leverkusen's 4-0 home win over Paderborn.
Moreira had failed to find the net since his summer move from Lyon but scored Leverkusen's first two goals and laid on one for Ezequiel Fernandez.
Patrik Schick also got a goal to move level with Niclas Fuellkrug atop the league goalscoring charts with nine goals.
In Saturday's late game, Schalke played out a scoreless home draw with Stuttgart.
Promoted in the summer, Schalke are yet to score a goal in five home matches.
Jonathan Burkardt scored the only goal as Eintracht Frankfurt beat Hoffenheim at home.
Frankfurt goalkeeper Noah Atubolu saved a first-half Andrej Kramaric penalty to keep his remarkable spot-kick record alive.
Atubolu has saved seven out of the 11 penalties he has faced, which is the best save percentage in the Bundesliga's 64-year history.

item.title: Nadal appointment confirmed at Real Madrid general assembly
item.description:
Retired tennis superstar Rafael Nadal joined Real Madrid's board of directors on Saturday after his appointment was ratified at the club's general assembly.
Nadal, a 22-time Grand Slam winner, has been an honorary club member since 2011 and shares a strong relationship with Madrid president Florentino Perez.
"I want to thank the president. When you named me honorary member it was very special, and today is one step further," said Nadal.
"For me, it's a great responsibility. Real Madrid is passed down from parents to children -- it's something that brings people together. And now, having this chance is an enormous opportunity."
President Perez said Nadal's appointment would help keep the club succeeding long into the future.
"His arrival is more than just the signing of an extraordinary figure -- it means that one of the greatest legends wants to share our future with us," said Perez.
"I am convinced that his presence will help us continue building the Real Madrid we want for the generations to come."
Nadal, 40, won a record 14 French Open singles titles in a glittering career.
In 2023 Nadal said one day he would like to be Madrid president, but did not know if he was qualified for the post.
Ahead of club elections this year Nadal distanced himself from reports that he would stand as a candidate. Perez triumphed in June, beating Enrique Riquelme.

item.title: Espi snatches late Real Madrid win over Celta Vigo
item.description:
Carlos Espi pounced to claim Real Madrid a late 2-1 victory over Celta Vigo in La Liga on Saturday, pulling Los Blancos level on points with leaders Barcelona.
The Spanish champions face Villarreal on Sunday looking to restore their three-point advantage over Jose Mourinho's in-form Madrid, who have won nine consecutive games across all competitions.
Espi, who has often provided vital contributions from the bench this season, helped Madrid complete a comeback at the Santiago Bernabeu stadium after Pablo Duran put the visitors ahead early on.
French superstar Kylian Mbappe missed a first-half penalty on a frustrating night for Madrid's top goalscorer.
However, Jude Bellingham pulled Madrid level before Espi netted in the 85th minute to claim the three points for his team.
"It's a dream day, I really wanted to (score) here at home in front of all the Madrid fans, it's a day I dreamed of, I'm really happy," Espi told Real Madrid TV.
"I try to do what the coach asks me, I'll give the most I can and take advantage of every minute that I'm given, and if I can help the team, then it's even better."
Mourinho began with Vinicius Junior on the bench, with the Brazilian eligible in La Liga again after a four-match ban for hair pulling, and the winger made contributions to both of Madrid's goals in a bright substitute appearance.
Celta Vigo took a surprise lead, through Spanish forward Duran in the sixth minute.
The Galicians carved open Madrid's defence with a slick attack, finished by Duran after Williot Swedberg played the ball through Dean Huijsen's legs and across the face of goal.
Madrid had a good chance to equalise when Yan Diomande whipped in a dangerous cross which Bernardo Silva sent wide with a diving header.
An even better one went begging when Mbappe won and then spurned a penalty.
The French forward was tugged back in the box by Javi Rodriguez but fired the resulting spot-kick high over the crossbar, his second penalty miss of the season.
Former tennis star Rafael Nadal, appointed to the club's board earlier in the day at Madrid's general assembly, pressed his hand to his forehead in disbelief.
- Super sub Espi -
Mourinho sent on Vinicius early in the second half as part of a triple change, with record signing Diomande switching to the right flank.
Vinicius was involved in Madrid's equaliser 10 minutes later, feeding Mbappe, who teed up Bellingham to power into the bottom corner for his fifth league goal.
Eduardo Camavinga sent a shot scuttling narrowly wide of the near post as Madrid tried to force their way in front, with Celta sitting ever deeper.
Eventually it came when Bellingham drove forward and laid the ball off to Vinicius, who swung in a cross to target man Espi, signed in the summer from Levante.
Although Celta goalkeeper Ionut Radu saved Espi's header, the forward stayed alert to tuck home the rebound.
It was Espi's third league goal of the season, each of which have led to Madrid claiming late victories.
"Madrid are a team with a lot of quality, they put you under the cosh... but we let go something that we thought we could take away (from here)," Celta's Duran told Movistar.
Earlier, Kike Salas struck late to save a point for Sevilla in a 1-1 derby draw against Real Betis.
Manuel Pellegrini's Betis, fourth, had taken the lead through Antony's deflected effort early in the second half.
However, hosts Sevilla, sixth, equalised in the 91st minute with Salas's low drive, which Betis goalkeeper Alvaro Valles somehow let squeeze past him.
"We let two points slip away in the final minutes with a completely avoidable goal," grumbled Pellegrini.
Valencia earned a 1-0 win at Rayo Vallecano to provisionally move out of the relegation zone. Alaves defeated Deportivo La Coruna 3-1 to climb up to eighth.

item.title: City stumble again in Fulham draw, Arsenal held by Newcastle
item.description:
Manchester City's winless Premier League run extended to four games after a damaging 1-1 draw against Fulham, while leaders Arsenal were held to a dramatic 2-2 draw at Newcastle on Saturday.
Third-placed City trail six points behind Arsenal as their title challenge wilts in the wake of a guilty verdict on widespread breaches of financial rules.
The club deny any wrongdoing but are likely to be hit with a severe points penalty, and possibly even relegation, unless they overturn the ruling on appeal.
After seven consecutive league wins to start Enzo Maresca's reign, the off-field uncertainty appears to have derailed City's quest to topple Arsenal.
Fulham had lost every meeting against City for the past 15 years but got their reward after striking early through Rodrigo Muniz at the Etihad Stadium.
City were furious that Erling Haaland's equaliser before half-time was controversially ruled out as the Norwegian was deemed to have kicked the ball out of the grasp of Bernd Leno.
Elliot Anderson's sweet strike saved City from a fourth consecutive defeat, but they were booed off after another disappointing display.
"Almost 80 percent of the goals we concede are in the first 20 minutes and it's for sure something we need to improve," said Maresca.
At St James' Park, Eberechi Eze put Arsenal ahead in the 33rd minute with a clinical close-range finish from Kai Havertz's pass.
But Newcastle rocked Mikel Arteta's men in the second half.
Harvey Barnes fired Newcastle's 49th-minute equaliser from William Osula's pass after Arsenal midfielder Martin Odegaard conceded possession cheaply.
When Dan Burn headed down from Lewis Hall's corner, Malick Thiaw pounced to give Newcastle the lead with a 62nd-minute tap-in.
Noni Madueke saved Arsenal from only their second league defeat this season, cutting inside for a low drive that eluded Lukas Hornicek's weak attempted save in the 78th minute.
Arsenal are six points above second-placed Brighton, who can close the gap with a win at Hull on Sunday.
"We needed to raise our level in the second half when the opponent had a reaction but we were below the level," said Arteta, who lost 'keeper David Raya to a second half shoulder injury.
"Individually we had some good performances but it was not enough."
- Chelsea on the rocks -
Leeds climbed to sixth place after coming from behind to stun Chelsea with a 4-1 win at Stamford Bridge.
Emmanuel Emegha's first Chelsea goal opened the scoring, but the Blues have now lost four of their last five matches to put manager Xabi Alonso under scrutiny.
Noah Okafor quickly levelled for Leeds before Dominic Calvert-Lewin put the visitors in front from the penalty spot.
Okafor delivered a thumping finish into the top corner and Brenden Aaronson delivered the final blow in stoppage time as Leeds savoured a famous win at the home of one of their historic rivals.
"We need to be tougher. It's something mandatory in this competition. Today we were in a fragile moment mentally," Alonso said.
Bournemouth climbed into the Champions League places as their sensational run continued with a 2-0 win over Nottingham Forest.
Evanilson struck for the sixth consecutive league game and Justin Kluivert added a second as the Cherries' winning run in all competitions stretched to nine games.
Teenager Luca Williams-Barnett was the star of Tottenham's 2-0 win over Ipswich as he netted on his first Premier League start before Dominic Solanke added a second to secure a fourth win in five for Roberto De Zerbi's men.
Thomas Frank's arrival at Crystal Palace failed to inspire a turnaround in the Eagles' fortunes as they lost 3-2 at Coventry to remain bottom of the table.
Sunderland frustrated Aston Villa in a 0-0 draw that lifted the Black Cats above Manchester United in the relegation zone.
Mauricio Pochettino will take charge of United for the first time at Liverpool on Sunday with the Red Devils second bottom of the table.

Jahangirnagar University admission 2026–27: Applications open, 1,848 seats available
item.description:
Applications for admission to the first-year undergraduate (honours) programmes at Jahangirnagar University (JU) for the 2026–27 academic year opened today, Sunday (22 November 2026).

Prospective students can apply online from 10:00 am. The application process will remain open until 11:59 pm on 15 December.

A total of 1,848 students will be admitted to Jahangirnagar University across 37 departments and institutes this year. Interested candidates must apply online in accordance with the guidelines published on the university’s admission website.

Admission test marks and grading system

According to the admission circular published on 16 November 2026, the university has lowered the GPA requirements for all units this year. The admission test will carry a total of 90 marks, with 40 as the pass mark.

The test will comprise 80 questions carrying a total of 90 marks, while another 10 marks will be determined by candidates’ SSC and HSC results. Each question will carry 1.125 marks, up from one mark previously. The negative marking will be 0.20.

HC suspends admission tests at all public universities until 31 December

Increase in seats

The university admitted students to 1,842 seats in the previous academic year. This year, it will admit students to 1,848 seats, an increase of just six. In 2025, the number of seats increased by 10.

Application fees

Applicants must pay the application fee online using a debit card, credit card or mobile financial service. The application fee for each of Units A, B, C and D is Tk 800.

The fee for Unit E, Unit C-1 and IBA-JU has been set at Tk 600 each. A service charge of 1.2 per cent will be added to the application fee. This charge applies to all units.

Eligibility criteria for applications

*Students who passed the Secondary School Certificate (SSC) or equivalent examinations in 2023 or 2024, and the Higher Secondary Certificate (HSC) or equivalent examinations in 2025 or 2026, are eligible to apply.

The minimum academic requirements for the SSC or equivalent and HSC or equivalent examinations (including the fourth subject) are as follows:

Dhaka University admission: 5 steps to complete the application

Unit A (Faculty of Mathematical and Physical Sciences and Institute of Information Technology)

To apply for Unit A, which covers the Faculty of Mathematical and Physical Sciences and the Institute of Information Technology (IIT), candidates must have a combined GPA of at least 7.50 in their SSC and HSC examinations, including the fourth subject.

They must also have a minimum GPA of 3.50 in each examination separately.

In the previous academic year, the requirement for applying to this unit was a combined GPA of 8.50, with a minimum GPA of 4.00 in each examination.

Unit B (Faculty of Social Sciences and Faculty of Law)

For Unit B, candidates from the science group must have a combined GPA of at least 7.50 in their SSC and HSC examinations, with a minimum GPA of 3.50 in each.

Candidates from the humanities, business studies and other groups must have a combined GPA of at least 6.50, with a minimum GPA of 3.00 in each examination.

Unit C (Faculty of Arts and Humanities and Institute of Comparative Literature and Culture)

For Unit C, which covers the Faculty of Arts and Humanities and the Institute of Comparative Literature and Culture, candidates from the science, business studies and other groups must have a combined GPA of at least 7.50, with a minimum GPA of 3.50 in each examination.

For candidates from the humanities group, the requirement is a combined GPA of 6.50, with a minimum GPA of 3.00 in each examination.

Unit C1 (Faculty of Arts and Humanities: Department of Theatre and Performance Studies and Department of Fine Arts)

Candidates must have a combined GPA of at least 6.50 in their SSC and HSC examinations, with a minimum GPA of 3.00 in each.

Unit D (Faculty of Biological Sciences)

Candidates must have a combined GPA of at least 8.00, with a minimum GPA of 3.50 in each examination.

BUET delays admission test by 2 weeks

Unit E (Faculty of Business Studies)

For Unit E, which covers the Faculty of Business Studies, candidates from the science group must have a combined GPA of at least 7.50, with a minimum GPA of 3.50 in each examination.

Candidates from the business studies, humanities and other groups must have a combined GPA of at least 6.50, with a minimum GPA of 3.00 in each examination.

Institute of Business Administration (IBA-JU)

Candidates from the science group must have a combined GPA of at least 7.50, with a minimum GPA of 3.50 in each examination.

Candidates from the business studies, humanities and other groups must have a combined GPA of at least 6.50, with a minimum GPA of 3.00 in each examination.

How to apply

Students must first visit Jahangirnagar University’s admission website and enter the required information to check whether they meet the minimum eligibility criteria.

DU admission applications opens, fees increased for four units

Applicants must then verify their own or their guardian’s mobile phone number. The password sent to that number should be saved for use during the application process and for accessing the website later.

An applicant can apply for multiple units using a single mobile phone number. However, the same number cannot be used to apply more than once for the same unit.

Applicants must go to their profiles and click on the ‘Upload Photo’ and ‘Upload Signature’ options to upload the required photograph and signature.

The recently taken, coloured passport-size photograph must be 300 × 300 pixels and no larger than 100KB. The signature must measure 300 × 80 pixels, with a maximum file size of 60KB. Both the photograph and signature must be uploaded in JPG or JPEG format.

RUET announces admission test date; 18,000 students to get chance to sit exam

Applicants must then select their preferred units from the list of units for which they are eligible and pay the prescribed application fees. In this way, a student can complete applications for one or more units, depending on their eligibility. Detailed payment instructions and steps are available on the university’s admission website.

Students who have passed O-level and A-level examinations must also apply by providing the required information and uploading scanned copies of their transcripts.

Admit cards and admission test schedule

Prospective students will be able to download their admit cards from 25 December. The admission tests are tentatively scheduled to take place between 10 and 21 January 2027.

However, no tests will be held on Fridays, Saturdays or public holidays. The final dates, examination schedule and seat arrangements will be published later on the university’s admission website.

item.title: Chinese vloggers' videos put Uttara's Tekpara in spotlight, but settlement remains unchanged
item.description:
A canal runs along the western edge of Sector 12 in Uttara, Dhaka. On one side are a planned residential neighbourhood, wide roads and rows of high-rise buildings. On the other are narrow alleys, tin-roofed houses and a densely populated settlement. The two sides look like two different worlds. Locally, this settlement is known as Tekpara.

Tekpara has recently come into the spotlight because of live videos recorded by Chinese nationals. For months, they have roamed the settlement's narrow alleys, filming their surroundings. They have recorded videos at tea stalls, along roadsides and even inside people's homes. In some of these videos, Tekpara has been presented as New Delhi, the capital of India. Questions have also been raised about the accuracy of information shared in these videos.

On 10 November, India's Ministry of External Affairs spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal reacted to the videos, calling for action against the Chinese nationals.

At a press conference, Jaiswal said, "It is unfortunate for both countries when people living in one country run down another country in this manner. Those involved in creating and promoting false narratives should understand that this also damages the credibility of their own country."

Although the videos by Chinese nationals have brought Tekpara into the spotlight, the settlement has a history of its own. How did a densely populated neighbourhood emerge in an area once surrounded by farmland and wetlands? Why has Tekpara remained deprived of basic civic amenities even as Uttara developed into a planned residential area? Who lives here, and how do they make a living?

Tekpara in videos, described as New Delhi

For several months, several groups of Chinese nationals have been visiting Tekpara and neighbouring areas in Uttara to record videos. Some have introduced Tekpara as New Delhi, the capital of India. They have also made derogatory remarks about the area's environment, people's lifestyles and food.

However, not all videos recorded by Chinese nationals have contained negative comments about Bangladesh. Some have also been heard making positive remarks about the country.

Local residents allege that the vloggers often enter their homes without permission while recording videos. This has caused irritation and anger among residents.

On 6 November, Prothom Alo published a report titled, Chinese citizens making live videos from morning till night, even going inside people’s homes.

Since 7 November, the Chinese nationals have no longer been seen livestreaming in different parts of Uttara. Local residents said they had not noticed Chinese nationals moving around the neighbourhood for several days.

Police at the local police station, meanwhile, said surveillance and law enforcement activities had been stepped up following media reports. Their activities have declined since then.

From elevated land to Tekpara

Tekpara is located at the northern edge of Uttara, within the jurisdiction of Turag Police Station.

Speaking to local residents, it was learnt that the area was largely agricultural land until before 2000. Rice, jute and various other crops were cultivated there. Compared with the surrounding low-lying areas, a section of what is now Tekpara stood slightly higher. Locals referred to this elevated land as 'tek'. The name of the neighbourhood gradually evolved into Fulbaria Tekpara.

Chinese vloggers no longer seen in Uttara, what were they doing?

According to residents, there were only five or six houses in the area around 1990. The rest of the land was used for cultivation. People also earned their livelihoods by fishing in the canal in front of the settlement.

One of the earliest homesteads belonged to Sheikh Nazimuddin, who died several years ago. His 55-year-old grandson Amir Hossain told Prothom Alo, "Our land was higher than the surrounding areas. That is why many people called it 'tek'. Eventually, the place came to be known as Tekpara."

Recalling the area's past, Amir Hossain said that although the surrounding areas were submerged during the 1988 floods, their homes remained above water because the land was elevated.

He remembers seeing rice and jute fields in the area during his childhood. Later, different companies began buying land and constructing buildings.

The canal was once teeming with fish

The canal in front of Tekpara also looked very different in the past. Its water was not as dirty and foul-smelling as it is today. Different types of boats used to ply the waterway, and many local residents earned their livelihoods by fishing.

Bedon Mia, 65, a local resident, told Prothom Alo that the canal water was once very clean. People made a living by catching fish. Steamers and launches used to travel along the river. Rice fields stretched as far as the eye could see on both sides. During the monsoon, surrounding agricultural land would be submerged, turning into large water bodies where local people caught fish.

Bedon Mia also described how land prices have increased over the years. According to him, a katha of land in Tekpara cost around Tk 100,000 in 2000. The price has now risen to Tk 8–9 million. In the planned residential areas of Uttara, however, a katha of land can cost between Tk 20 million and Tk 30 million.

More than 300 families, most of them tenants

While only a handful of families lived in Tekpara in the past, the settlement is now home to more than 300 families. Most are tenants. Many landowners in the area live in different affluent neighbourhoods of Uttara.

During a visit to Tekpara on 21 November, this correspondent found a densely populated settlement along a small canal. Most houses have tin walls and roofs, while some are semi-pucca structures. The internal roads are narrow and unpaved. Some areas are damp, and rubbish is scattered around the houses. There is also a noticeable lack of adequate drainage and hygienic sanitation facilities. The canal in front of the settlement emits a foul smell.

A large proportion of the residents have moved to Dhaka from different districts in search of work. Some drive auto-rickshaws, while others run small shops. Many women work as domestic helpers in nearby homes. They have settled here because rents are relatively low.

Idris Ali, a tenant in the area, told Prothom Alo that house rents are lower here than in neighbouring areas, which is why he lives in Tekpara with his family.

He moved to Dhaka with his family around 2017 because they had no land in their village. He has lived in Tekpara ever since and now works as a rickshaw puller.

Planned Uttara, an old settlement next door

Tekpara was not the only area that once had vast stretches of open fields, wetlands and low-lying land. Much of Uttara was once similar, with agricultural activities and fishing in the wetlands.

Later, to ease Dhaka's housing shortage and reduce pressure on the city, the then Dhaka Improvement Trust (DIT) took an initiative to develop a planned satellite town in the northern part of the capital.

In 2002, a research paper by Mamun Rashid, then an assistant professor at the Department of Architecture of Bangladesh University of Engineering and Technology (BUET), was published on the university's website under a training programme of Sweden's Lund University.

The study, titled Housing at Uttara Model Town in Dhaka City, outlines the history of Uttara's planned urban development.

According to the study, a feasibility survey for planned urbanisation of the area was conducted in June 1965. The project was initially named 'North Satellite Township'. Its name was changed to Uttara Residential Model Town in 1980.

In 1987, the Rajdhani Unnayan Kartripakkha (RAJUK) was established, replacing the Dhaka Improvement Trust.

The first phase of development in Uttara was completed in 1992. Around 6,000 plots were allocated on 950 acres of land during this phase.

Development of the second phase began in 1992. It was completed in 1998, with 5,315 plots allocated on 438 acres of land.

A study titled Communities in a Growing Megacity: A Pathway to Urban Sustainability for Uttara, Dhaka, presented at the International Green Architecture Conference in 2018, provides details of the third phase of Uttara's development plan.

According to the study, planning for this phase began in 1999–2000. The project was approved by the Executive Committee of the National Economic Council (ECNEC) in May 2000. Land acquisition began in 2000–2001, while development work started in 2004.

The implementation of different phases of Uttara's residential projects gradually transformed the surrounding areas as well. Planned residential neighbourhoods, high-rise buildings and commercial establishments replaced agricultural land and wetlands. Land prices rose, and people's lifestyles changed.

Despite being adjacent to Uttara's planned residential areas, Tekpara continues to lag behind in terms of civic amenities. However, Dhaka North City Corporation (DNCC) has said it has plans to develop the area.

SM Shafiqul Rahman, chief town planner (additional charge) of DNCC, told Prothom Alo that a development plan has already been undertaken for Uttara's extended or adjoining areas, including Tekpara, Fulbaria and Nalbhog.

Residential projects developed in different phases have transformed Uttara and its surrounding neighbourhoods. Agricultural land and wetlands have given way to high-rise buildings, roads have been widened, and land prices have increased several times over.

But Tekpara remains outside this transformation. Although only a canal separates the two neighbourhoods, the gap in living conditions is considerable. Narrow alleys, tin-roofed houses and a lack of basic civic amenities remain part of everyday life in this settlement, right next to a planned urban area.

item.title: Class-I admission (2027): Apply on 1 Dec, digital lottery 15 Dec
item.description:
The applications for admission into Class-I for the 2027 academic year in all private schools and colleges across the country will commence on 1 December.

The application window will remain open until 10 December. Students for Class-I will be selected via online digital lottery at 11:00 am on 15 December.

The Directorate of Secondary and Higher Education (DSHE) issued directives regarding this on 19 November. The guidelines signed by the Director (Secondary) of the Directorate, detailed the admission process across secondary, lower secondary and attached primary levels in private schools and school and colleges nationwide including those in Dhaka city.

According to the directives, applications for Class-I admission will be accepted exclusively online at http://gsa.teletalk.com.bd.

The application fee is set at Taka 110 which must be paid via SMS using a Teletalk prepaid mobile connection.

Applicants may select up to five schools in order of preference, subject to availability. If an applicant chooses both shifts of an institution that operates on a double-shift basis, each shift will count as one of the five choices. It will not be possible to select the same school or shift more than once.

Meanwhile, admissions for classes-II through IX must be conducted through written examinations, managed by the respective institution’s own admission committee.

In this process, the 2027 admission policy for private schools and colleges must be followed. Furthermore, instructions have been provided to ensure adherence to various quotas and catchment area requirements.

The directives also stated that the heads of institutions must publish an admission notice specifying the number of vacant seats available at their institutions.

The notice must clearly state the date and time for the submission of application forms.

The DSHE has confirmed that the selection of students for Class-I will be conducted through an online digital lottery. The admission process must be conducted under the constant guidance and supervision of the Admission Oversight and Monitoring Committee.

At the same time, transparency and accountability must be ensured throughout the entire admission process.

Detailed guidelines regarding the completion of admission applications and other admission-related procedures can be found in the ‘Secondary Circular/Order’ section of the DSHE website (www.dshe.gov.bd), as well as on the Teletalk website (www.teletalk.com.bd).

All relevant educational institutions have been instructed to carry out the admission process in accordance with the admission policy prescribed by the Ministry of Education.

item.title: Scars left in Narail's Bendarchar village
item.description:
In Kalia upazila of Narail, houses and shops belonging to several leaders and activists, including BM Kabirul Haque Mukti, a former MP of the activities-banned Awami League, have been attacked, vandalised, looted and set on fire following the murder of two leaders of the Krishak Dal and Jatiyatabadi Samajik Sangskritik Sangstha (JASAS), associate organisations of the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP).

This incident took place last Friday from the afternoon until midnight in the village of Bendarchar. When firefighters arrived at the scene, they saw 20 to 30 houses on fire.

Besides this, houses of three former MPs of the Awami League were also attacked and vandalised in Patuakhali. These incidents occurred between 10:00 pm on Thursday and 9:00 pm on Friday.

Meanwhile, repeated clashes broke out between BNP and Awami League leaders and activists in Bera Municipality of Pabna on Friday.

Vandalism and fire in Kalia

Earlier on Wednesday, two people were killed in an attack on a BNP motorcycle rally by activists of the Awami League in Kalia Upazila. They were Sohail Rana, general secretary of the Kalia Upazila Bangladesh Jatiyatabadi Samajik Sangskritik Sangstha (JASAS), and Shahinur Islam, general secretary of the Municipal Krishak Dal.

Victims from Bendarchar village claim that on Friday afternoon, people from the BNP suddenly attacked the houses of the Awami League leaders, including Kabirul Haque Mukti and former municipal mayor Mushfiqur Rahman.

At that time, around 50 houses and shops in Bendarchar village were vandalised, looted, and set on fire. Additionally, a similar attack occurred at the house of Krishnapada Ghosh, the general secretary of the Upazila Awami League, in the greater Kalia area.

However, the local BNP denied the allegations of attacking and setting fire to any houses. Kalia Upazila BNP's General Secretary SM Wahiduzzaman told reporters that the allegations of house attacks and arson are completely baseless. The notion that these were done in the presence of BNP leaders is fictional.

Saturday, Kalia Upazila Nirbahi Officer (UNO) Md Jinnatul Islam told Prothom Alo that before dusk on Friday, several houses, including that of the former MP, and 15-20 rooms were vandalised.

Five to six rooms were set on fire. They have been able to confirm attacks on the houses of former MP BM Kabirul Haque and Upazila Awami League General Secretary Krishnapada Ghosh. However, there were no casualties. The administration is not sure who carried out the attacks, but the matter is being investigated.

Police statement on the attacks

Meanwhile, a press release from the Narail District Police stated that the circulating reports of attacks, vandalism, and looting on Hindu homes in Bendarchar village are false and fabricated.

The previously recorded or AI-generated videos published by the Awami League activists on social media are misrepresenting the government and the country's image both domestically and internationally.

The press release states that there is no Hindu settlement in the Bendarchar area. No attack on any Hindu family or their businesses took place.

In response to the allegations of attacks on Hindu settlements, Kalia Upazila BNP General Secretary Wahiduzzaman said that in the last national elections, 90 per cent of the Hindu community here voted for the BNP. The Hindu community is with the BNP, and they are with them.

He further stated, "I saw on Facebook that over 200 homes were attacked; this is completely false."

The police press release noted that due to the murder of two BNP leaders, enraged relatives of the deceased and others gathered in Bendarchar village around 4: 45 pm on Friday.

They attacked the houses of several Awami League activists involved in the murder and left. The police from Kalia police station arrived at the scene and brought the situation under control. The situation is now normal, and additional police have been deployed there, the release mentioned.

Narail Superintendent of Police (SP) Mohammad Al Mamun Shikdar told Prothom Alo on Saturday afternoon over the phone that relatives and supporters of the two deceased BNP leaders attacked and vandalised three to four houses in the village. The area is not Hindu-dominated. The way it is being portrayed is not how it actually is.

Fire service statement on the arson

Kalia Upazila Fire Service Station Officer Humayun Kabir told reporters that the fire started around 4:00 pm on Friday. Due to obstacles and lack of security, they could not reach there immediately. They arrived at the scene around 8:00 pm.

While many houses were burning at the time, the fires were not very intense. They extinguished some fires while others went out on their own. There were fires in 20 to 30 houses, each having three to four rooms, so the actual number could be higher.

On-site at Bendarchar village

Saturday, around 10:30 am, this reporter visited Bendarchar village. Upon entering the village, a woman was seen leaving the area with some belongings in a pedal van, accompanied by a small child.

On condition of anonymity, she said, “There were three cows, they took them. There is not a single item left in the house. TVs and refrigerators, 10 blankets, all the things in two trunks, nothing is left in the three rooms. There's not even a quilt to cover ourselves. They destroyed the motor from the tube well.” She also alleges that her sister-in-law was threatened with rape.

Another woman named Mukta Khanom stated, “The incident happened after the Friday prayer. Around 400 people came. They vandalised and filled vehicles with whatever was there. These were all locals from Kalia, BNP people. They did the same throughout Bendarchar.”

Apart from the elderly, no other men were seen at home in the village. Many women were seen leaving their homes to go elsewhere.

item.title: Mahi wears khadi sari in Miss Universe, celebrates motherhood and motherland
item.description:
The 75th Miss Universe competition is underway in Puerto Rico in the Caribbean, with actress Samira Khan Mahi representing Bangladesh. She took to the stage for the national costume round at 5am Bangladesh time on 22 November.

Mahi’s national costume, designed around the theme of motherhood, had been revealed the day before. Wearing a red and white sari, a traditional outfit closely associated with Bengali women, she walked onto the stage with confidence, presenting a glimpse of Bangladesh through her attire.

A story of motherhood woven into Cumilla khadi

Mahi’s sari was made from Cumilla khadi fabric and designed by designer Bishwajit Mazumder. Bishwajit and his team also created the circular artwork worn on Mahi’s back, inspired by the theme of motherhood.

Bishwajit said, “We had very little time to design the sari. I had only three days. I spent the first two days developing the theme and creating the circular artwork celebrating motherhood, which Mahi carried on her back today. The sari itself was made in just one day.”

The international stage of Miss Universe offers an opportunity to showcase a country's culture and identity. Bishwajit said he chose to highlight motherhood with that in mind.

He said people also refer to their homeland as their mother, so he sought to connect the idea of mother and motherland. The circular artwork on Mahi’s back depicted a woman’s journey from childhood to becoming a mother and in the final stage of her life, finding refuge in her daughter’s embrace. Through the artwork, he sought to portray a story of affection and love passed down through generations.

Bishwajit said the sari was made from 16 yards of cotton khadi. To ensure Mahi could walk comfortably on stage and wear it with ease, the sari was pre-stitched into a ready-to-wear outfit. The border featured embroidered water lilies in a traditional kolka motif, while the sari also incorporated block-print designs.

Traditional jewellery inspired by Bengali mothers

Mahi paired the sari with gold-toned jewellery. Although gold jewellery is traditionally worn across much of South Asia, her collection drew particular inspiration from traditional Bengali ornaments.

The jewellery was designed by Tanwy Kabir, owner and designer of jewellery brand Canvas. She, too, had only seven days to complete the collection. During that time, nine artisans collectively spent 880 working hours crafting the pieces.

Tanwy said, “The traditional ornaments worn by mothers in our region in the past — Sita haar, kantha haar, bala and kantana jhumka — inspired this collection through their familiar designs, elegance and emotional significance. Through each piece, I wanted to revisit our roots, heritage and the emotions intertwined with the adornment of our mothers.”

Each piece was handcrafted by artisans with meticulous attention to detail. Beyond preserving the tradition of Bengali jewellery, Tanwy said she also wanted to showcase the skills, artistic sensibilities and craftsmanship of local artisans through the collection.

Mithila arrives in Puerto Rico with the national costume

As Mahi was selected Miss Universe Bangladesh 2026 at the last moment, she could not take her national costume with her. Her friend and Miss Universe Bangladesh 2025 Tanjia Zaman Mithila took charge of preparing the costume and accessories.

Speaking from Puerto Rico, Mahi said, “Mithila apa thought of the national costume, just as she did with everything else. Having a friend and elder sister like her meant I could manage and organise so much despite having so little time.”

Mithila arrived in Puerto Rico a day before the national costume round, carrying the outfit with her. All the elements of the costume were made in Bangladesh. To make it easier to transport, the circular artwork on Mahi’s back was constructed in nine separate pieces. The artwork depicting motherhood was made using wood, foam, fabric and shola.

Combining indigenous khadi, water lily motifs, traditional jewellery and the story of motherhood, Mahi’s national costume brought together Bangladesh’s culture, craftsmanship and emotional heritage in a single presentation.
