item.title: Court denies bail to ex-education minister Nahid
item.description:
A Dhaka court has rejected the bail petition of former education minister Nurul Islam Nahid in a murder case filed over the death of madrasa student Sadikul Islam during the July 2024 uprising.
Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate Mohammad Sefatullah passed the order after a hearing on Monday, prosecution department Sub-Inspector Helal Uddin said.
Advocate Sathi Saha, representing Nahid, sought bail, arguing that her client had retired from politics and all professional activities long before the incident. She also cited his age and health, telling the court that he was no longer physically capable of leading or joining street processions and would not abscond if released.
However, prosecutor Muhammad Shamsuddoha Sumon opposed the bail petition. After hearing both sides, the court rejected the application.
Nahid was arrested from his residence in Sector 13 of Uttara West last Wednesday around 2am. He was sent to jail the following day in connection with the murder case.
According to the case statement, Sadikul took part in the movement in Uttara West on July 19, 2024. Around 3pm that day, leaders and activists of the Jubo League and Bangladesh Chhatra League allegedly attacked protesters, chasing and beating them indiscriminately before opening fire.
Sadikul was shot in the abdomen and taken to Uttara Adhunik Medical College Hospital, where he died while undergoing treatment on July 20.
On September 15, 2024, Ashraf Siddiqui filed a murder case with Uttara West Police Station over the incident.

item.title: Who is top criminal ‘Sweden Aslam’?
item.description:
Sheikh Mohammad Aslam, better known as Sweden Aslam, was one of the most notorious names in Dhaka's underworld during the 1990s.
He was accused of murder, extortion and establishing criminal dominance in areas including, Karwan Bazar, Farmgate, Rajabazar, Tejgaon and Sher-e-Bangla Nagar. Allegations that he used disguises, wore a bulletproof jacket and continued to control criminal activities from prison added to his notoriety.
Immigration police detained him at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport around 2:30am on Sunday as he was preparing to board a Thai Airways flight to Thailand. He was later handed over to the Dhaka Metropolitan Police's Detective Branch (DB).
DB Additional Commissioner Md Shafiqul Islam confirmed that Aslam was in custody and said he would be interrogated. Police suspect he planned to travel to Malaysia via Bangkok.
According to DB officials, more than 100 complaints, including allegations of extortion, have been submitted against him to the DMP commissioner. Police have also received claims that he operated at least five torture cells, which are being investigated.
Aslam's family is from Chhatia in Dhaka's Nawabganj Upazila. He studied at Tejgaon Polytechnic School, now Tejgaon Government High School. His rise in the capital's underworld reportedly began around 1986-87, initially in Rajabazar, Indira Road and Farmgate.
He came to prominence in 1987 over allegations that he killed a teenager named Shakil inside Nazneen School in East Rajabazar. His rivalry with the Rana group, which controlled criminal activities in Karwan Bazar and nearby areas, intensified after 1990.
In 1996, Aslam reportedly brought Pichchi Hannan, a key member of the rival group, into his camp. That year, Aslam was accused of involvement in the murder of Rana in front of the Superstar Hotel on Kazi Nazrul Islam Avenue. His influence subsequently spread across Karwan Bazar, Tejturi Bazar, Tejgaon and surrounding areas.
The nickname “Sweden” reportedly came from his first wife, Iti, who lived in Sweden. Aslam is said to have lived there with her for several years before returning to Bangladesh.
Aslam was arrested on May 26, 1997, following the murder of Jubo League leader Mahmudul Haque Khan Galib, who was killed outside his home in Tejkunipara on March 23 that year. Galib's wife, Shaheda Nasrin Shampa, filed a case over the killing.
Reports say 22 cases were filed against Aslam, including nine murder cases, as well as cases involving abduction, extortion and firearms. He was also accused of maintaining contact with associates and influencing criminal activities from prison. Reports over the years alleged that mobile phones were recovered from his cell and that he threatened complainants and witnesses. These claims have not all been independently established.
After spending 27 years in prison, Aslam was released on bail from Kashimpur High Security Central Jail on September 3, 2024, at the age of 62.
Following his release, his name resurfaced in media reports about disputes over extortion in Karwan Bazar and Tejgaon, including discussions surrounding the murder of former Swechchhasebak Dal leader Azizur Rahman Musabbir. However, his alleged involvement in those incidents remains unproven.
DB officials say efforts to detain him had been under way for about a month. Sources also said his passport had been blocked to prevent him from leaving the country.

item.title: Workers block road in Ashulia; 28 factories declare holiday
item.description:
Authorities have declared a general holiday at 28 garment factories in Ashulia, Savar, near Dhaka, until 1:15pm on Monday amid ongoing labour unrest over demands for a revision of the minimum wage.
The development came as some workers reported for duty but refused to work, while a group of protesters blocked a road in the Nishchintapur area, attempted to vandalize a bus and targeted nearby factories.
Police fired tear gas shells and sound grenades to disperse the protesters and bring the situation under control.
According to the Industrial Police, workers at several factories arrived at their workplaces on Monday morning but refrained from working and remained inside the premises. The work stoppage prompted factory authorities to declare general holidays.
Mohammad Mominul Islam Bhuiyan, superintendent of police of Ashulia Industrial Police-1, said general holidays were initially declared at nine garment factories due to the work stoppage. In five other factories, workers remained inside the premises without performing their duties.
The number of factories declaring holidays later rose to 28, with the closures remaining in effect until 1:15pm.
Meanwhile, tension flared in the Nishchintapur area of Ashulia on Monday morning, when a group of workers blocked the Abdullahpur-Baipail road.
According to witnesses, after a general holiday was declared at the New Age factory in Nishchintapur, a group of workers came out of the facility and occupied the road.
At one point, they allegedly attempted to vandalize a bus and attack other factories that were still operating in the area.
Police subsequently deployed tear gas shells and sound grenades to disperse the protesters.
There were also allegations that workers leaving nearby factories after completing their shifts were assaulted.
One worker claimed the attacks were driven by resentment towards employees who had reported for duty instead of joining the work stoppage.
Some workers were reportedly pulled off rickshaws and beaten, the worker alleged.
Meanwhile, 22 factories have been closed indefinitely under Section 13(1) of the Bangladesh Labour Act amid the ongoing labour unrest.
The factories include those belonging to the Hamim, Envoy, Knit Asia and Next Collection groups.
Two other factories have separately declared general holidays.
The decisions to close the factories under Section 13(1) were taken at different times, depending on the workers' unrest and the situation at each facility.

item.title: Gopalganj remains calm after rumours trigger late-night show of force
item.description:
Security vigilance has been stepped up in Gopalganj following the spread of rumours on social media claiming that the Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) would carry out a “massacre” in the district on Sunday night.
The rumours prompted announcements over mosque loudspeakers in Gopalganj town and several surrounding unions, urging residents to come out and resist the alleged threat.
After 10pm, thousands of people took to the streets carrying makeshift weapons, including sticks, machetes, hockey sticks, spears, shields and pikes. They staged a show of force, although no violent incidents were reported.
The announcements were made in Majhigati, Kathi, Durgapur, Raghunathpur, Latifpur, Haridaspur and Chandradighalia unions, among other areas.
Some local leaders of the Awami League and its affiliated organisations, whose activities are currently prohibited, later posted messages on their social media accounts clarifying that the claims about a planned BGB operation were false.
However, the clarifications did little to ease public concern, and many residents remained on the streets until midnight before returning home.
Despite the late-night tension, the district's overall law and order situation remained stable, with no reports of major incidents.
Transport services across Gopalganj were operating normally, and long-distance buses departed according to schedule. Government and private offices, courts, banks and insurance companies also remained open, as did shops and other business establishments.
However, an underlying sense of anxiety has kept some people away from the town centre, while business activity has declined, despite daily life largely returning to normal.
In a statement issued on Sunday night, the BGB said a coordinated smear campaign was being carried out against the force through Facebook pages and other social media accounts.
The campaign was spreading baseless claims about a so-called operation or massacre in Gopalganj, creating confusion and panic among residents, the statement said.
It added that fabricated and inflammatory information, including false claims involving senior BGB officials, was being circulated while members of the public were being incited to organise and attack BGB personnel.
The force described the claims as baseless and malicious, and condemned attempts to spread panic and destabilise law and order by circulating rumours involving a state security agency.
The BGB said its members were performing their duties professionally to maintain peace and stability in Gopalganj and prevent sabotage. It also warned that anyone involved in subversive activities would face immediate legal action.
At the same time, the force assured residents that there was no reason for the general public to be alarmed.
At the request of the Gopalganj district administration and under the directives of the Ministry of Home Affairs, two BGB battalions have been deployed in the district to maintain law and order.
Alongside other law enforcement agencies, BGB personnel are patrolling key roads and thoroughfares in the presence of a magistrate to prevent sabotage.
Security at vital installations has also been strengthened in coordination with the district administration, Ansar and police.
The BGB headquarters' monitoring cell is keeping a close watch on the situation using drones, body-worn cameras and other surveillance equipment, the statement added.

item.title: 98 BGB platoons deployed in Dhaka, several districts
item.description:
A total of 98 platoons of the Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) have been deployed in Dhaka and several districts to maintain law and order, ensure public safety and prevent any untoward incidents.
The deployment includes two battalions in Gopalganj, as well as personnel in Dhaka, Gazipur, Narayanganj, Mymensingh, Faridpur, Chittagong and Cox's Bazar.
Acting on the directives of the Ministry of Home Affairs, BGB personnel are carrying out their duties in coordination with the respective district administrations and other law enforcement agencies.
The force has stepped up security and surveillance at key installations, industrial zones and other important locations to prevent unrest, violence and activities that could threaten public safety.
Meanwhile, BGB headquarters is using technology-driven surveillance to monitor and coordinate the situation on the ground. The monitoring includes real-time footage from drones, body-worn cameras and other technological equipment.
Alongside their regular border duties, BGB personnel are also assisting in maintaining internal law and order, the force said.
The BGB said it remained committed to protecting public safety and property, ensuring the smooth movement of people and taking precautionary measures to address any unforeseen developments.

item.title: 57 platoons of Ansar deployed in nine districts
item.description:
A total of 57 platoons of Ansar Battalion members have been deployed across nine districts, including Gazipur, to maintain law and order and ensure public security.
With the deployment of four additional platoons in Gazipur, one of the country's major industrial hubs, the total number of Ansar Battalion members deployed there has risen to 17 platoons.
The information was disclosed in a press release issued by the Bangladesh Ansar and Village Defence Force on Monday.
According to the release, the four additional platoons were deployed in Gazipur to maintain law and order and keep industrial production running. The members are on alert to prevent sabotage, disorder and activities that could threaten public safety.
Acting on directives from the Ministry of Home Affairs, the members are also performing security duties at key state installations and ensuring smooth traffic movement on highways across the nine districts.
The district-wise deployment includes 17 platoons in Gazipur, 15 in Gopalganj, five in Faridpur, four each in Narayanganj, Khulna, Madaripur and Shariatpur, and two each in Satkhira and Mymensingh.
The release further said regular patrols and checkpoint operations are being conducted under the direct supervision of senior officials, while suspicious movements are being monitored. The members remain prepared to respond immediately to any untoward situation.
The Bangladesh Ansar and Village Defence Force reaffirmed its commitment to protecting public life and property and maintaining peace and order across the country.

item.title: Garment workers protest as wage board meets in Dhaka
item.description:
Garment workers staged a protest outside the Labour Building in Bijoynagar, Dhaka, on Monday, demanding a monthly minimum wage of Tk32,000 for workers in the readymade garment sector.
The demonstration began shortly after the third meeting of the Minimum Wage Board started at around 11:30am at the building in Segunbagicha.
Activists and leaders from several workers' organisations gathered outside the building, chanting slogans in support of their demand.
Among the participating groups were the Garment Workers Trade Union Centre, Bangladesh Garment Workers' Solidarity, the National Platform for Protecting Garment Workers and Industry, the Garment Workers' Rights Movement and the Garment Workers' Council.
Meanwhile, representatives of factory owners and workers were attending the board meeting, chaired by District and Sessions Judge Syed Azad Subhani.
Factory owners were expected to submit their proposed new wage structure at the meeting.
The board's third meeting had previously been postponed on November 16 due to unavoidable circumstances.

item.title: DU extends admission application deadline to Nov 28
item.description:
The University of Dhaka has extended the deadline for online applications for undergraduate admission in the 2026-27 academic session by three days, giving prospective students until November 28 to apply.
The previous deadline was November 25. The decision was taken considering the publication schedule of students' re-evaluation results, Professor Dr Mohammed Almujaddade Alfasane, the university's pro-vice-chancellor (administration), told Dhaka Tribune.
Online applications opened at noon on November 11, in line with the university's previously announced schedule.
Students will be admitted through five units: IBA, Science, Arts, Law and Social Sciences, Business Studies, and Fine Arts.
According to the admission schedule, the IBA unit test will be held on December 5, the Science unit test on December 12, the Arts, Law and Social Sciences unit test on December 19, the Fine Arts unit test on December 22, and the Business Studies unit test on December 26.
Except for the IBA unit, all admission tests will take place from 11am to 12:30pm. The IBA test will be held from 10am to 12pm.

item.title: Public university admission tests can proceed, rules top court
item.description:
The Appellate Division of the Supreme Court has stayed a High Court order suspending admission tests at all public universities, including the University of Dhaka, until the results of re-evaluated answer scripts and re-examinations of this year's HSC and equivalent examinations are published.
The Appellate Division passed the order on Monday, following an appeal filed by the Ministry of Education against the High Court order., reports Bangla Tribune.
The hearing was conducted by a bench led by Chief Justice Zubayer Rahman Chowdhury.
Attorney General Barrister Ruhul Quddus Kajal represented the state in court, while Senior Advocate Barrister Abdul Qaiyum and Barrister Kamarun Mahmud Deepa appeared for the writ petitioners.
Earlier, on November 18, the High Court directed all public universities, including the University of Dhaka, to suspend admission tests until the results of answer script re-evaluations and supplementary examinations for students who failed this year's HSC and equivalent examinations were published.
The order came from a High Court following an initial hearing on a writ petition.
The results of the re-evaluations and supplementary examinations are scheduled to be published on December 23.
The court also issued a rule asking why the publication of the admission test schedule for public universities for the 2026-27 academic year, under the University Grants Commission's (UGC) directive (Annexure-B), before the publication of the supplementary and re-evaluation results of the HSC examinations should not be declared beyond legal authority and unlawful.
Later, the writ petitioner, Barrister Kamarun Mahmud Deepa, said around 350,000 students had applied for re-evaluation of their answer scripts.
She said the UGC had decided to begin admission tests at all public universities from December 5, before the supplementary and re-evaluation results of these students were published.
Considering the interests of the 350,000 students, the High Court had suspended admission tests at all public universities until December 31, she added.
Following the order, the Ministry of Education filed an appeal with the relevant section of the Appellate Division's Chamber Judge Court on November 19.
After hearing the appeal, Chamber Judge Justice Md Rezaul Haque declined to stay the High Court order and scheduled the matter for hearing before the full bench of the Appellate Division on Monday.

item.title: Top criminal Aslam now in DB custody
item.description:
Sweden Aslam, once known as one of Dhaka’s top criminals, is now in the custody of the Detective Branch (DB) of the Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP).
Md Shafiqul Islam, additional commissioner (DB) of the DMP, confirmed the matter to Dhaka Tribune on Monday morning.
Immigration police detained him at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport in Dhaka early Monday while he was attempting to leave the country for Thailand on a Thai Airways flight.
Ziauddin Ahmed, deputy commissioner of the Tejgaon division DB, said immigration police detained Aslam at around 2:30am.
He said law enforcement agencies had been searching for Aslam for a long time and that several allegations were pending against him.
Aslam, also known as Sheikh Aslam, was arrested on January 31, 2005, and spent nearly 19 years in prison.
Following the fall of the Awami League government on August 5, 2024, he was released from jail on September 4 that year.

item.title: Festival of Lights fills Fine Arts Faculty with colour and warmth
item.description:
The premises of the Faculty of Fine Arts at the University of Dhaka were illuminated by thousands of lamps and candles on Sunday evening as students celebrated the “Alok Projjolon Utsab 1433” (Festival of Lights 1433).
The area came alive with colourful decorations, fireworks, music and cultural performances as students organised the festival on Sunday, with a pledge to dispel darkness and evil and move towards the light.
The event began at 5:30pm on the faculty premises, drawing students from various departments. Lamps and candles were lit at different spots across the campus, while colourful decorations transformed the entire area. Fireworks, musical performances and cultural programmes added to the festive atmosphere.
With enthusiastic participation from students, the festival turned into a gathering of the university community. Alongside Fine Arts students, students from other departments and visitors also joined the celebrations.
The Festival of Lights is an artistic and cultural event organised by the Faculty of Fine Arts.
Through the lighting of lamps and candles, it symbolises the triumph of light over darkness and a commitment to positive change. Rooted in art, culture and tradition, the event brings the university community together in a festive atmosphere.

item.title: Titon murder: DB seeks 7-day remand for Sweden Aslam
item.description:
The Detective Branch (DB) of police has sought a seven-day remand for alleged top criminal Sweden Aslam for questioning in a case over the murder of Khandaker Nayeem Ahmed Titon in Dhaka's New Market area.
Inspector Irfan Khan of the DB's Ramna Zonal Team and also the investigation officer in the case filed the remand petition on Monday.
Confirming the development, Sub-Inspector Moktar Hossain of the prosecution devision said the remand plea would be heard by Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Md Ismail.
Sweden Aslam was arrested at the airport late Sunday night while allegedly attempting to leave the country.
According to the case statement, Titon was released on bail on August 13, 2025. After his release, he regularly communicated with his elder brother, Khandaker Saeed Akhtar Ripon, through various mobile applications.
During their conversations, Titon reportedly told his brother that he had caused the family significant financial losses and was trying to ensure that they would not face further embarrassment. He also expressed his intention to work honestly and lead a decent life.
A few days before the incident, Titon told Ripon that he planned to buy a tender schedule, adding that he hoped to earn a living through legitimate work.
On April 26,2026 Titon informed his brother over the phone that he was involved in a dispute over the lease of the Basila cattle market with Enamul Hasan Helal, alias Pichchi Helal; Badal, alias Killer Badal or Kaila Badal; Shahjahan; and Rony, alias Bhangari Rony.
The following day, Titon told Ripon that the group had called him and that he intended to resolve the dispute through mutual understanding.
At around 11pm on April 28, Ripon learned from several people that his younger brother had been shot in front of Shahnewaz Hall, near a banyan tree, in the New Market Police Station area.
Titon collapsed on the road in a blood-soaked condition. He was rushed to Dhaka Medical College Hospital, where doctors declared him dead.
On April 29, Ripon filed a murder case with New Market Police Station against unidentified suspects.
In the complaint, he alleged that a group of armed assailants arrived on motorcycles and, as part of a planned attack involving seven unidentified individuals, opened fire indiscriminately on Titon over previous enmity. The attack took place on the paved road near the banyan tree in front of Shahnewaz Hall. Titon collapsed with bullet wounds and was later declared dead at the hospital.
Both Aslam and Titon were named among 23 alleged top criminals on a list published by police in 2001, during the BNP-Jamaat alliance government.
DB officials said at least 100 complaints, including allegations of extortion, had been lodged against Sweden Aslam at the Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) Commissioner's Office. He is also accused of operating at least five torture cells.
Police had been stepping up efforts to arrest him over the allegations, prompting him to allegedly attempt to flee the country, DB officials said.
Aslam's rise in the criminal underworld began around 1986-87 in the capital's Rajabazar and Indira Road areas.
During the 1990s, he came into the spotlight for his alleged attempts to establish control over the underworld in several parts of Dhaka, including Karwan Bazar, Tejgaon, Tejgaon Industrial Area and Sher-e-Bangla Nagar.
Aslam faced 22 cases at different times, including nine murder cases. He was convicted in several cases, including those involving firearms.
After spending more than 19 years in prison, he was released on September 3, 2024, following the fall of the Awami League government amid the July mass uprising.
Meanwhile, Titon and his brother-in-law, another alleged top criminal, Sanjidul Islam Emon, were associated with the Haris-Joseph group, a criminal network based in Mohammadpur. Titon was reportedly active in Dhanmondi and Hazaribagh.
Emon is also accused of being involved in widespread extortion and land grabbing in Mohammadpur, Dhanmondi and Hazaribagh.

item.title: Ziaul Ahsan case proceedings may be broadcast live on BTV
item.description:
The prosecution will begin presenting closing arguments in the case against Major General (retd) Ziaul Ahsan at International Crimes Tribunal-1 on Tuesday, with the proceedings potentially broadcast live on Bangladesh Television (BTV) and Facebook.
Prosecutor Gazi MH Tamim confirmed the information on Monday.
Tamim said the arguments in Ziaul Ahsan's case would begin on Tuesday. Subject to the tribunal's permission, the proceedings would be broadcast live on BTV and the prosecution's Facebook page.
Earlier, following the conclusion of witness testimony on November 22, International Crimes Tribunal-1 scheduled Tuesday for the presentation of arguments.
On December 17, 2025, the prosecution filed a formal charge against Ziaul, bringing 3 allegations over the enforced disappearance and killing of more than a hundred people.
Subsequently, on January 14, the tribunal framed charges and ordered the start of the trial.
Ziaul Ahsan was most recently the director general of the National Telecommunication Monitoring Centre (NTMC), the national agency responsible for telecommunications surveillance.
He was arrested in mid-August 2024, following the fall of the Awami League government.

item.title: BGB steps up border surveillance with searchlights, drones in Mymensingh
item.description:
The Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) has stepped up surveillance along the border under its Mymensingh sector, using more than 50 CCTV cameras, over 20 searchlights, night-vision devices and drones to prevent illegal crossings, smuggling and human trafficking.
The force has also warned that anyone attempting to enter or leave Bangladesh illegally, including fugitives or controversial individuals, will be arrested.
Colonel Nasir Uddin, commander of the BGB's Mymensingh sector, made the remarks at a press conference on Monday afternoon at the Shaheed Mushtaq Mahmud Multipurpose Shed at the sector headquarters in Mymensingh.
He said the BGB remained on high alert to prevent illegal movement across the border and was carrying out its duties to protect national sovereignty, border security and the lives and property of the people.
The Mymensingh sector covers approximately 243 kilometres of the border, with personnel from three battalions deployed along the stretch to maintain security around the clock, he said.
The force has identified high-risk and sensitive areas and strengthened security measures to prevent illegal infiltration, smuggling and sabotage.
Nasir Uddin said plans were underway to install an additional 65 CCTV cameras and 33 searchlights to strengthen surveillance.
In remote and riverine areas, the BGB is using all-terrain vehicles (ATVs). In addition to the four regular patrols conducted by each Border Outpost (BOP), special patrols are also being carried out, he added.
Responding to questions about the activities of individuals who had fled to India near the Haluaghat border in Mymensingh and the Maheshkhali border area in Netrakona, the sector commander said the BGB had received some information and was verifying it through intelligence surveillance and field-level operations.
The force was also coordinating with other law enforcement agencies, he said.
So far, no suspicious activity had been detected in those areas, but the BGB was not overlooking any information, Nasir Uddin said.
He added that information was being verified and cross-checked in coordination with other law enforcement agencies, the Directorate General of Forces Intelligence (DGFI) and the National Security Intelligence (NSI).
At the press conference, the BGB said it had thwarted 11 attempts to push 141 people across the border illegally within the Mymensingh sector between January 1 and November 23 this year.
During the same period, four human traffickers were arrested, and 13 Bangladeshi victims of human trafficking were rescued.
Legal proceedings are also underway against 58 people accused of involvement in human trafficking, the BGB said.

item.title: South Korea's SK Group keen to invest in LPG, LNG terminals at Matarbari
item.description:
South Korean conglomerate SK Group has expressed its interest in investing in the construction of liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) and liquefied natural gas (LNG) terminals in the Matarbari deep-sea port area, seeing potential to develop it into an energy hub like Ulsan in South Korea.
A high-level delegation of the group conveyed the interest during a meeting with Prime Minister Tarique Rahman at his office in the Secretariat on Monday, said PM's Deputy Press Secretary Shahadat Hossain Shadhin.
During the meeting, the delegation made a detailed presentation to the prime minister on its proposed investment in the LPG and LNG terminals at Matarbari.
The delegation said Matarbari had the potential to emerge as an energy hub similar to Ulsan, a major industrial and energy centre in South Korea.
Tarique welcomed the group's interest in investing in Bangladesh's energy sector and said his government was working to simplify and accelerate the process of attracting foreign investment.
He urged the delegation to move quickly with the proposed projects and directed the authorities concerned to take necessary steps to ensure government support for their implementation.
The SK Group delegation praised the government's investment-friendly policies and expressed its keen interest in exploring investment opportunities in Bangladesh.
Finance and Planning Minister Amir Khosru Mahmud Chowdhury, State Minister for Power, Energy and Mineral Resources Aninda Islam Amit, and Invest Bangladesh Chairman Ashik Chowdhury were present.
Youngone Corporation Chairman Kihak Sung and SK Gas Chief Executive Officer and President Kyunyeol Song were also among the delegation members.

item.title: India captain Gill calls for cricket to relax saliva ban
item.description:
India captain Shubman Gill said Monday he wants the ban on using saliva to shine the cricket ball to be relaxed after a drawn Test against New Zealand played on a lifeless pitch.
Only 24 wickets were taken across five full days of play while 1,327 runs were scored, including a record 720-9 by India, the highest innings in Tests in New Zealand.
A usually fast and bouncy Basin Reserve was low, slow and lifeless by the second morning.
"If you are not shining the ball or if you are not able to maintain the ball, especially on wickets like this, it makes the job of the bowlers very difficult," Gill said after New Zealand ground out 239-5 in their second innings to rescue a draw.
"I do believe that players, teams should be allowed to use saliva. It was a rule that was made during Covid. I think we are long past that.
"If the ball is going soft after 25, 30 overs or it's going out of shape, and you are also not able to maintain the ball and use saliva then it's very difficult."
New Zealand captain Tom Latham said Gill was right in his assessment of the ball during the match.
"Probably apart from day one, throughout the game the ball tended to get soft," Latham said.
"But in terms of rules and conditions, certainly from a saliva point of view, I'm not sure that will change (with) what the world's been through.
"You've got to find a way and in the current day and age and the rules that we currently have, we work as hard as we can to keep the ball in as good a condition as possible."
Both captains said the match ball has seemed softer in recent years and provided a challenge to fielding units to maintain and encourage swing.
In Wellington the issue was exacerbated by a dry wicket that didn't break up and got progressively slower as the match wore on.
Gill said it was "not a great Test wicket", while Latham said it was "not your traditional Basin surface".
New ground staff took over the Basin Reserve pitch during the New Zealand winter, but had their preparation time hampered due to flooding, Cricket Wellington staff told AFP, leading to a lifeless track.
India and New Zealand now head to Christchurch for the second and deciding Test starting Friday, where both captains expect a more typical green, grassy and seamer-friendly wicket.

item.title: Pochettino demands response from 'painful' Man Utd debut
item.description:
Mauricio Pochettino said Manchester United must harness the pain from a 4-0 thrashing by Liverpool on Sunday into positive change despite feeling aggrieved by Leny Yoro's eighth-minute red card.
Pochettino's reign got off to a nightmare start when Yoro was controversially sent off for bringing down Alexander Isak.
United never recovered as Liverpool instantly took advantage when Dominik Szoboszlai smashed home the resulting free-kick.
Defeat leaves United still second bottom of the Premier League and at risk of relegation from the English top flight for the first time since 1974.
"It's so painful, we feel pain for that defeat, but we need to keep the head up and translate that anger to an energy to start to work from tomorrow for the next game," said Pochettino.
"We need to accept the reality and we need to be responsible. We need to be united, we need to be all together and I think we feel disappointed because it's clear that after eight minutes, I think, the plan was in the bin."
Isak had taken a heavy touch and the ball appeared to be running through to United goalkeeper Senne Lammens before contact was made by Yoro.
"I'm not going to change what happened and being respectful is always important," added Pochettino.
"At the same time I need to defend my club and say what I feel. I feel like that was an action that everyone who plays football can see was clearly not a red card."
A repeat of United's 7-0 thrashing at Anfield three years ago appeared on the cards when Florian Wirtz doubled Liverpool's lead inside 13 minutes.
However, Pochettino's introduction of Harry Maguire and switch to a back five helped stem the bleeding until teenager Rio Ngumoha and Victor Munoz rounded off the rout in the second half.
"It hurts a lot. It's a difficult moment for us but we are the only ones who can get out of that situation," said United captain Bruno Fernandes, who raged against the decision to dismiss Yoro.
"There are too many referees on the pitch and too many on VAR taking so long to see to make a mistake like this that can change the game," added the Portuguese international.
"It's not because of them we conceded the goal from the free-kick, but it changes the game completely."
Victory lifts Liverpool up to fourth in the table and within seven points of leaders Arsenal.
Andoni Iraola savoured the adulation coming his way at full-time and believes his side should have run up an even bigger margin of victory.
Isak and Bradley Barcola were guilty of wasting a number of big chances either side of half-time.
"It's difficult to enjoy in the Premier League, normally you suffer even if you win, but I think we could celebrate at half-time and enjoy it a little bit," said Iraola.
"We have missed some clear chances today. In other games you will remember those chances, but today we've controlled the game and everything was happening around the (United) box."

item.title: Rain delays toss in 2nd Bangladesh-South Africa Test
item.description:
The toss for the second and final Test between Bangladesh and South Africa was delayed due to rain at Super Sports Park in Centurion today.
The hosts South Africa are leading the two-match series 1-0, following a nine-wicket victory in the first Test in Johannesburg.
Both teams, however, would have to bring up changes for the second Test because of the injuries. South Africa had already named their playing XI, bringing in Tony de Zorzi for injured regular captain Temba Bavuma, while fast bowler Anrich Nortj‚ replaced fellow pacer Dane Paterson.
Bangladesh didn't name their playing XI as of now. But senior batter Mushfiqur Rahim is out with a groin injury, and fast bowler Hasan Mahmud misses out due to an elbow problem. Therefore, they would have to bring up at least two changes to the squad.

item.title: New Zealand battle to 239-5 to draw first India Test
item.description:
New Zealand rescued a draw on the final day of the first Test against India in Wellington on Monday, surviving 120 overs in a fighting display to finish 239-5 at the close.
India had declared their first innings on a mammoth 720-9 midway through the fourth day with a lead of 352 runs after New Zealand made 368.
Daryl Mitchell (49 not out) and Glenn Phillips (26 not out) batted India into submission on a lifeless Basin Reserve pitch.
The two-Test series moves to Christchurch on Friday with all to play for in the decider.
"You know, we're pretty happy," New Zealand captain Tom Latham said of the draw.
"Obviously India played fantastically well. We were under pressure, only a couple of results at play and to be in the position where a couple of guys put their hands up was great."
India had needed five wickets in the final session for victory, but there were few alarms for the New Zealand batsmen.
Captain Shubman Gill shook hands with Phillips and Mitchell an hour before the scheduled close to agree a draw after turning to part-time bowlers Yashasvi Jaiswal and Dhruv Jurel in a last, desperate attempt for a breakthrough.
"All of our fast bowlers bowled almost 50 overs in the match," Gill said of his decision.
"If there was anything in the wicket and if they felt they could get the batsmen out, if there was a plan in place, they executed it, but there wasn't enough in the wicket.
"Ten or 15 overs wouldn't have made a difference."
New Zealand, who started the final day at 119-2, lost two wickets in the first session to give India hope of victory.
Devon Conway, who top-scored with 65, was the first man out just before the first drinks break.
He edged off-spinner Washington Sundar onto his pads, with wicketkeeper Rishabh Pant taking a fine diving catch.
Rachin Ravindra, 27 overnight, soon followed for 37, slashing Prasidh Krishna to KL Rahul at gully after a 129-ball vigil.
India's bowlers were relentlessly accurate on a lifeless Basin Reserve pitch, where the wind picked up for the first time in the match, allowing Sundar to find the drift that deceived Conway, who added only six to his overnight score.
New Zealand crawled to 206-5 at tea, still 146 runs from making India bat again, having scored just 49 runs in the session and lost one wicket, Tom Blundell for 15.
Blundell was given out on review for a faint edge off pace bowler Anshul Kamboj, well taken by Pant standing up to the stumps.
For India, Krishna took 2-23 from 19 overs, while Jasprit Bumrah had 1-42 from 20 overs.
India had declared on a mammoth 720-9 in their first innings on Sunday -- the highest Test score on New Zealand soil -- after six of their top seven made fifties, with Rahul going on to 136 and Pant 128.
New Zealand's Henry Nicholls scored an unbeaten 175 in their first innings 368, while Phillips made 118.

item.title: Atalanta grab dramatic draw with Inter, Ramos scores in Milan rout
item.description:
Atalanta rescued an extraordinary late 4-4 draw against Inter Milan on Sunday as the champions fell three points off the Serie A title pace despite Francesco Pio Esposito's hat-trick, while AC Milan and Juventus claimed big wins.
Inter looked comfortable in Bergamo when Petar Sucic's penalty gave them a two-goal cushion in the 76th minute after Esposito's treble, but Charles De Ketelaere's second goal of the night and a stoppage-time Franck Kessie penalty salvaged a point for La Dea.
It marked only the third time Inter have dropped points in the league this season but kept Cristian Chivu's side in third place, one point behind Roma and three adrift of leaders Lazio.
AC Milan stayed in the title mix by going fourth, two points behind Inter, with a 5-1 win over Frosinone, while Juventus moved into the top six by thrashing Venezia 4-0 in Turin.
Inter's result continued a theme of defensive frailty, having conceded 17 goals in 12 league games this season.
"We managed to always have a two-goal lead, then we failed to show maturity in the final moments," Chivu told DAZN.
"It's hard to explain, we weren't able to manage and maintain the lead we created. We have thrown away two points, but we will learn the lesson and move on."
Esposito struck twice in the first half, pouncing on a deflected ball in the box to sweep home the opener before doubling Inter's lead by heading home from a corner.
Eljif Elmas quickly got one back for the hosts to keep the game alive, but Esposito took his third in composed fashion early in the second half, marking his eighth goal in five games for club and country.
De Ketelaere proved the catalyst for Atalanta's fightback, pulling a goal back with a header and firing home a powerful finish either side of Sucic's spot-kick.
That set up a thrilling conclusion as Atalanta chased what had seemed an unlikely point, which they claimed when a penalty was awarded for handball that Kessie calmly converted.
- Ramos scores in Milan rout -
Milan returned to the top four as Goncalo Ramos ended his goal drought in a 5-1 thrashing of Frosinone to seal back-to-back wins for the first time in over a month.
Ruben Amorim's side got off to a flying start with a Gabriele Calvani own goal and a composed Ramos strike inside 19 minutes.
Amorim accused his players of "not helping Ramos" ahead of the game after the Portugal international scored just twice in his first 11 league games following a 74-million-euro ($86 million) summer move from Paris Saint-Germain.
His third goal of the season was met with a loud roar from the San Siro crowd after he was teed up by France international Adrien Rabiot, who became the first Milan midfielder since Kaka in 2004 to notch a goal or assist in seven consecutive league games.
The visitors soon hit back through Patrizio Masini, but Milan pulled clear in the second half with some lethal counter-attacking as Ardon Jashari, Alphadjo Cisse and Christian Pulisic struck to complete the biggest victory of the Amorim era.
"Frosinone are all about full pressure. I understood that coming to San Siro with a lot of points, they would be really brave," Amorim told DAZN.
"We changed a little bit the way we play the game because of the opponent, and it was a good night for us."
- Spalletti relieves pressure -
Juventus moved up to sixth thanks to a second-half surge in a 4-0 win over Venezia in Turin.
Coach Luciano Spalletti faced scrutiny after an underwhelming start to the season, with Antonio Conte linked with a return to his former club during the international break.
But Spalletti celebrated becoming just the sixth coach to reach 600 Serie A games with a resounding win, despite his team being booed off at the break following a goalless first half.
Nick Woltemade came off the bench at half-time to score one goal and set up another for Teun Koopmeiners, before a Juan Cabal header and Randal Kolo Muani penalty wrapped up an 18-minute blitz.
Milutin Osmajic scored a double in a 2-0 win for Genoa at Sassuolo and Bologna were held to a 1-1 draw.

item.title: Alcaraz downs Zverev to win ATP Finals for first time
item.description:
Carlos Alcaraz won the ATP Finals with a 6-2, 7-6 (9/7) victory over world number one Alexander Zverev in the title match in Turin on Sunday.
After becoming the youngest man to complete a career Grand Slam at the start of the season with victory in the Australian Open, the 23-year-old has bookended an up-and-down year with a first title at the season-ending showpiece tournament.
Alongside Roger Federer, Andre Agassi and Novak Djokovic, Alcaraz now forms part of an exclusive list of men to have won all four majors and the ATP Finals.
With his illustrious compatriot Rafael Nadal never managing to win the season-ending tournament, Alcaraz became the first Spanish champion since Alex Corretja in 1998.
"It's been an amazing week. I couldn't finish the week in a better way, so I'm really proud," Alcaraz said after capturing his sixth title of the year.
"I've been through really difficult moments with myself, with my team, and we could go through everything. I'm playing great tennis, so for me, lifting this trophy is something that I've been chasing for a really long time. It means the world to me," he added of the hamstring issue he suffered earlier in the tournament.
A wrist injury had caused Alcaraz to miss a good chunk of the middle of the season and following that victory in Melbourne he failed to add to his seven major titles.
But since returning in August, he has enjoyed a blistering end to the year, winning his last 14 matches to capture trophies at the Vienna Open, the Paris Masters for the first time and now the elusive ATP Finals.
He lost in the season-ender's final to Jannik Sinner last year, but with the injured Italian having curtailed his season, Alcaraz found himself again in the Turin title match against a world number one.
Zverev, a two-time ATP Finals champion, broke his Grand Slam duck this season by claiming the French and US Opens, catapulting him above Alcaraz and Sinner to the top of the rankings.
- Topsy-turvy -
The top two seeds in Italy, Alcaraz and Zverev were a cut above the rest all throughout the tournament, both topping their respective pools with three wins from three.
The first set of Alcaraz's semi-final win over Ben Shelton was the only frame either player had dropped all week.
Indeed Zverev had marched into the final without dropping a service game, but he was mightily tested straight out of the traps by Alcaraz as the world number three forced three break points in the very first game before the German dug in to hold.
Alcaraz was not so wasteful two games later, however, as he broke Zverev to love when the 29-year-old overcooked a mid-court forehand.
Zverev forced break-back points in the next game but, after failing to convert, he was left to rue his luck even further as the Spaniard broke to 30 to grow his lead to 4-1.
Zverev wiped out one break but Alcaraz was nonetheless firmly in the ascendancy and pounced for a third time on the Hamburg native's serve in an entertaining seventh game which saw Zverev dejectedly chuck his racquet to the floor after netting a smash from an Alcaraz tweener lob.
A netted backhand by Zverev -- his 19th unforced error of the match -- on Alcaraz's first set point then brought an end to a surprisingly sloppy opening frame.
Both players exchanged breaks in the second set as it went the distance.
The Murcian took a 3-0 lead in the tie-break before Zverev won the next six points to bring up three set points.
But the Spaniard struck back to wipe them out before getting a mini-break to bring up championship point on his own serve.
The first went begging when he whipped a forehand into the tramlines but he brought up a second with a drop-shot and sealed the title with a backhand.

item.title: West Bengal to be renamed Paschim Banga, proposal to be tabled on December 9
item.description:
West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari on Monday announced that a proposal to rename the state as “Paschim Banga” will be tabled in the state Assembly on December 9.
The decision was taken at a cabinet meeting chaired by Adhikari at the state secretariat, Nabanna.
Speaking to reporters after the meeting, Adhikari said the proposed name would be used in English as well as Bengali, with the spelling retained as “Paschim Banga.”
“The proposal to rename West Bengal as ‘Paschim Banga’ will be tabled in the House on December 9,” he said.
If passed by the Assembly, the resolution will be sent to the central government for approval and the necessary parliamentary and legal procedures.
The winter session of the West Bengal Assembly is scheduled to run from December 4 to 14.
The proposed change follows an earlier attempt by the Trinamool Congress (TMC) government, led by Mamata Banerjee, to rename the state as “Bangla.”
In July 2018, the state Assembly unanimously passed a resolution proposing the name change. However, the central government did not approve the proposal despite repeated requests from the state government.
The BJP leadership has argued that “Paschim Banga” reflects the historical circumstances surrounding the creation of the state during the Partition of Bengal in 1947.
On June 20, 1947, Shyama Prasad Mookerjee, founder of the Bharatiya Jana Sangh, moved a proposal in the Bengal Legislative Assembly supporting the partition of Bengal. The state was subsequently divided, with its eastern part becoming East Bengal, which later became Bangladesh.
The BJP government has also observed June 20 as Paschim Banga Divas, marking the historical events surrounding the partition.
The latest proposal would formally seek to replace the name West Bengal with Paschim Banga in official usage, subject to approval by the central government.

item.title: Houthi media says 10 dead in Saudi attack on Yemen port city
item.description:
Houthi media said Monday that a Saudi attack had killed 10 people and wounded more than 20 in Yemen’s key port city of Hodeida.
The Iran-backed fighters, who control swathes of Yemen including Hodeida, are battling a Saudi-led coalition that backs Yemen’s internationally recognized government.
The strike targeted a building belonging to Yemen’s Public Telecommunications Corporation, the Houthis’ Almasirah television channel wrote on X.
The channel had earlier reported the toll as four dead before raising the number several hours later.
Saudi Arabia did not immediately comment on the report.
It came a day after the Saudi-led coalition said it had intercepted a ballistic missile launched towards Saudi Arabia’s western Red Sea coast.
That region is home to major oil installations which Houthi fighters have attacked in recent weeks along with strikes on airports and military sites.
Yemen, which has been embroiled in more than a decade of civil war, was sucked into the US-Iran conflict in July when a truce between the Houthis and the Saudi-backed government unraveled.
Since then, hostilities have left more than 1,600 people dead and over 300,000 displaced in the country, the poorest on the Arabian Peninsula, according to the latest UN toll.

item.title: Modi offers flood-hit Nepal $1.6 bn aid package
item.description:
Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi offered a $1.6 billion “development cooperation” package to neighboring Nepal on Monday in the wake of devastating Himalayan floods.
“We express our deep condolences for the loss of lives caused by the devastating floods in Nepal in August,” Modi said, standing alongside his Nepali counterpart Balendra Shah in New Delhi.
“To support Nepal’s reconstruction, and give fresh momentum to its long-term development, we announce a development cooperation package worth 240 billion Nepali rupees ($1.6 billion),” he said.
India did not immediately give specific details of what the development package included.
Shah was given a military honor guard parade at the presidential palace in New Delhi, on his first trip to a neighboring country since taking office in March.
The rapper-turned-politician came to power following a wave of youth-led anti-corruption protests in September 2025.
Shah, 36, wearing his trademark sunglasses and dressed in black, was given a bear hug by Modi, 76, dressed all in white.
Unlike his predecessors, Shah had initially refrained from foreign visits since becoming prime minister.
His first overseas trip was to New York in September, where he addressed the United Nations General Assembly as Nepal reeled from a deadly tsunami-like flood, triggered by a high-altitude glacial mountain collapse, that killed more than 1,400 people and left 5,000 missing.
Nepal, a largely rural country that contributes little to global greenhouse gas emissions, estimates reconstruction will cost $4.78 billion.
Shah said it showed the “imperative to address the challenges of climate change through collective action.”
In October, the United Nations’ climate loss and damage fund agreed the modest sum of $20 million in aid to Nepal -- the maximum amount countries can request in a single application -- and the first time it has set aside money for any country.
Nepal, a landlocked Himalayan nation of 30 million people, has long had to balance its relations with its two giant neighbors, India and China.
“Our commitment will be to help affected families rebuild their lives, create new opportunities and further strengthen Nepal’s capacity to deal with future disasters,” Modi said.
India is Nepal’s largest trading partner, accounting for more than 60 percent of its imports, worth $8.6 billion, while China accounts for 13 percent, or $1.8 billion, according to World Bank figures.
Modi said the two countries’ relationship was rooted in “shared history, culture and deep people-to-people ties,” as he unveiled a joint vision document for cooperation.
The two leaders also launched projects including a cross-border railway, a 669-megawatt hydropower plant, an expanded petroleum pipeline and a new oil storage terminal.
“May the friendship between Nepal and India be one where trust stands as tall as the Himalayas, cooperation flows as continuously as a river, and the prosperity of both nations flourishes beneath our shared sky,” Shah added.

item.title: Mahdi Amin: No conditions set during PM's meeting with NCP delegation
item.description:
A delegation of the National Citizen Party (NCP) met the prime minister on Monday, but no conditions were set during the meeting, Mahdi Amin, an adviser to the prime minister and spokesperson for his office, said.
“The NCP delegation presented its points, while the prime minister outlined the government's position,” he said.
Mahdi made the remarks while speaking to journalists at the Secretariat at 3:20pm on Monday.
He said the government would fully implement the July Charter, including the note of dissent.
The government's position on reforms was clear, Mahdi said, adding that the prime minister had reiterated in parliament that the government would implement the reforms outlined in its election manifesto and promised during election campaign rallies, including those related to the note of dissent.
He also said a record number of ordinances had been converted into laws during the first session of the National Parliament after the formation of the government.
Reform was an ongoing process, and the government remained committed to fulfilling all its election pledges, he added.
Responding to a question about the need for a new form of political unity, Mahdi said there was no need for one.
He said a sense of unity had emerged during the July mass uprising, when people from all walks of life, social classes and professions had come together to bring down the fascist regime.
That unity continued to exist, he said, adding that the people of Bangladesh were the ultimate owners of state power.

item.title: From Tk3,000 to Tk10cr: How Shafeen Built Zaituni Foods
item.description:
When Shafeen Shafayet borrowed Tk3,000 from his mother, he did not have a detailed roadmap for building a company. There was no office, no team, and no established customer base. He simply had the determination to create something of his own.
That small investment became the foundation of Zaituni foods, a natural products brand focused on black seed oil and wellness products. According to the founder, the company has crossed Tk10 crore in total sales through years of experimentation, customer understanding, and continuous improvement.
However, the journey from a small online venture to a growing brand was not easy. Before achieving growth, there were months of uncertainty, slow sales, financial pressure, and moments when continuing the business seemed difficult. The company’s progress came from adapting to challenges, improving quality, and building customer trust step by step.
Finding the Right Opportunity
Shafeen grew up in a middle-class family where education and hard work were highly valued. His father worked as a school teacher, while his mother was employed in a government job. During his intermediate studies, he developed an interest in entrepreneurship and started exploring opportunities to build something independently.
With financial support from his mother, he started his first venture by selling Turkish olive oil through personal networks.
“Although I started with olive oil, my goal was to work with a local product that had scientific value and could create long-term benefits for people,” he said.
While working with olive oil, he began studying the natural products market more closely. He noticed that consumers were increasingly looking for products they considered healthier, safer, and more reliable.
During this period, he researched black seed oil and identified a market gap. Although the product was already familiar among Bangladeshi consumers, there was a lack of brands that could consistently provide quality, transparency, and customer confidence.
Recognising this opportunity, he decided to make black seed oil the core product of Zaituni foods.
The Difficult Beginning
The early stage of the business was challenging.
Sales were unpredictable, and managing expenses with limited capital became difficult. There were months when customer orders were inconsistent and profitability remained uncertain.
“The first eight months were almost without profit. Sometimes I had to save money from one month to manage the next month’s expenses,” he said.
At the same time, he was continuing his studies, creating additional pressure. Balancing academic responsibilities with business operations required discipline and commitment.
Like many entrepreneurs, he also faced moments of doubt. There were times when closing the business appeared to be the easier option. However, instead of quitting, he focused on improving the product, understanding customers, and adapting his strategy.
Those early struggles became an important learning experience that shaped the foundation of Zaituni foods.
The Turning Point Through Digital Storytelling
A major shift came when Shafeen created a video featuring content creator Rifat Ratul.
The video gained strong attention online and generated significant customer responses. According to him, it resulted in several lakh taka worth of olive oil orders within a short period.
The experience changed his understanding of marketing. He realised that customers do not connect only with products; they connect with the story, purpose, and trust behind a brand.
From that point, content became a major part of Zaituni foods’ growth strategy. Instead of focusing only on product promotion, the company started educating customers and building stronger relationships with its audience.
Building a Trusted Brand
As Zaituni foods expanded, the founder realised that long-term success required more than sales. A strong brand identity was essential to create customer trust and recognition.
Although the company gained wider online recognition around 2024, he believes branding should have received greater attention from the beginning.
For him, a business is not only about selling products. It is about creating a relationship with customers and building confidence in what the brand represents.
“A business is not only about selling products; it is also about creating trust among customers,” he said.
Customer feedback has played a major role in shaping the company’s decisions. Through messages, phone calls, and direct communication, the team understands customer expectations and develops products based on real needs rather than temporary market trends.
Maintaining Quality and Expanding Reach
For natural product businesses, maintaining consistent quality is one of the biggest challenges.
The founder believes that products may appear similar in the market but can differ significantly in quality. Ensuring a reliable standard requires careful sourcing, testing, and monitoring.
During the sourcing process, several samples were evaluated and rejected before selecting suitable products. Since black seed oil remains the company’s main product, maintaining its quality has become one of Zaituni foods’ key priorities.
Starting as an online-based business, the company is now expanding beyond digital platforms. Its products are available at selected locations, including Feni and Banasree in Dhaka, with plans to increase retail availability across Bangladesh.
The company is also exploring opportunities in Middle Eastern markets.
For the founder, the next phase is not only about increasing sales but also about making quality natural products more accessible to customers.
Beyond Business: A Tech-Driven Future
While building Zaituni foods, Shafeen has continued to invest in his passion for science, technology, and innovation.
From an early age, he was recognised as a sharp student with a strong interest in technology. Coming from a science background and having returned from ISSB, he had aspirations of pursuing higher studies at globally recognised institutions such as Harvard, MIT, or Cambridge through scholarships.
Although entrepreneurship changed the direction of his formal academic journey, it never stopped his pursuit of knowledge.
Alongside managing and expanding the company, he completed advanced studies in Nuclear Engineering through MIT OpenCourseWare and continues exploring emerging fields such as Machine Learning and Quantum Computing through online learning platforms.
For him, these efforts are not about collecting degrees or preparing for a conventional career path. Instead, they represent a personal commitment to using technology as a tool for future entrepreneurship.
“I am not pursuing these advanced studies to get a job or simply earn higher academic degrees. These are my personal efforts to empower my entrepreneurial journey with technology and take it to a globally competitive level.”
His long-term vision extends beyond natural products. He aims to explore opportunities in energy and other globally impactful technology sectors by combining entrepreneurship with advanced fields such as Quantum Computing and Machine Learning.
The Road Ahead
The next goal for Zaituni foods is to build a stronger nationwide distribution network, introduce more black seed-based products, and explore international markets.
However, his ambition is not limited to business expansion alone. He wants to create ventures where entrepreneurship, science, and technology come together to solve larger challenges.
The story of Zaituni foods began with Tk3,000 and a willingness to experiment. Its growth did not come from a single breakthrough moment but from years of small decisions — choosing the right product, listening to customers, improving quality, building trust, and remaining consistent during difficult periods.
For Shafeen, crossing Tk10 crore in sales is not the finish line. It is another milestone toward building a Bangladeshi company with global ambitions, driven by innovation, technology, and a commitment to creating wider impact.

item.title: Bus, truck set on fire in separate incidents in Narayanganj
item.description:
Miscreants set fire to a bus and a truck carrying garment waste in two separate incidents in Narayanganj early Monday.
No casualties were reported.
The first incident occurred around 12:15am, when an Anabil Paribahan bus parked in the Giridhara area of Signboard on the Dhaka-Chittagong Highway was set on fire.
The second incident took place around 4:45am near a CNG-run auto-rickshaw stand in the Stadium area of Fatullah on the Dhaka-Narayanganj Link Road, where a truck loaded with garment waste was torched.
According to local sources, several people arrived in the Signboard area in an auto-rickshaw around 12:15am and threw a petrol bomb at the parked bus, setting it ablaze.
Bus owner Russell said the vehicle operated on the Narayanganj-Gazipur route. He said the fire broke out after the workers had parked the bus for the night and returned home. The vehicle was completely gutted.
In the second incident, two men arrived on a motorcycle and threw a petrol bomb at the parked truck near the CNG stand in the Stadium area of Fatullah before fleeing.
Truck driver Mamun said he had brought garment waste from Chittagong to Narayanganj. He said they parked the truck beside the Link Road around 4am and went to sleep. After being alerted to the fire, he woke up and found the truck ablaze. Several lakh taka worth of goods were destroyed.
Fire Service sources said two units from the Signboard fire station rushed to the scene after receiving reports of the bus fire and brought it under control in about 20 minutes.
Two units also worked for around one and a half hours to extinguish the fire in the truck, bringing it under control at around 6:30am.
Fatullah Model police station Officer-in-Charge Mahbub Alam said those involved in the incidents would be identified and arrested.
However, he said the location of the bus fire in Signboard might fall under the jurisdiction of Jatrabari police station and that the matter was being investigated further.
